scenes.say: Three green days and you're sure it's a trend. In a random series, it isn't.
Recency bias: whatever just happened feels like what will keep happening.
Code builds a purely random up-down series of {n} days and finds every run of {k} in a row.
scenes.note: Simulation: random series, not a model of any market

scenes.say: Next day keeps the same direction {same} of the time.
In random data, the last few days tell you nothing about tomorrow. Your brain still sees a story.
Before you conclude, ask: would pure randomness look exactly like this?
